name: Steak Fajitas
desc: Marinated strips of skirt steak and peppers seared in a hot skillet and finished with reserved lime-cumin marinade.

source.title: Steak Fajitas Recipe
source.evidence: Identical ingredient list and amounts (2 lb steak, 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp lime juice, 1/2 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp cumin, pinch of cayenne) and the same jar marinade split in thirds between steak, vegetables, and the pan.

ingredients.raw: 2 lb skirt, flank, sirloin, or hanger steak, sliced into 1/2-inch strips
ingredients.item: skirt, flank, sirloin, or hanger steak

ingredients.raw: 1 red bell pepper, seeded and sliced into thin strips
ingredients.prep: seeded and sliced into thin strips

ingredients.raw: 1 green bell pepper, seeded and sliced into thin strips
ingredients.prep: seeded and sliced into thin strips

ingredients.raw: 1 medium yellow onion, peeled and sliced into thin strips
ingredients.prep: peeled and sliced into thin strips

steps: Put the steak strips in one zip-top bag and the peppers and onion in another.
Put the olive oil, lime juice, chili powder, cumin, cayenne, salt, pepper, and garlic in a jar with a tight lid and shake until combined.
Pour a third of the marinade over the steak and a third over the vegetables; keep the last third in the jar. Seal the bags and refrigerate at least 1 hour or up to overnight.
Heat a large skillet (cast iron is best) over medium-high heat. Add the vegetables and cook until crisp-tender, about 5 min. Move them to a plate.
Add the steak strips to the same skillet in a single layer, in batches if needed, and sear until browned and cooked through, 7-10 min total (at least 145°F).
Return the vegetables to the skillet with the reserved marinade from the jar and toss until heated through, about 1 min.
Serve with the warm tortillas and toppings.
tips: The jar third never touches raw meat, which is why it can go straight into the pan; discard the marinade left in the steak bag.
